name: PhD Programs (Jefferson College of Life Sciences)
detailsNote: The admissions FAQ gives a December 1 priority deadline without a year, so it is shown as a published date. That page also quotes statistics for an older (2018) cohort, which were not used.
summary: PhD programs at the Jefferson College of Life Sciences with a flexible entry pathway. Students do lab rotations in the first year, then choose a thesis advisor and one of six PhD programs.

publishedDeadlines.label: Priority application deadline (year not stated)
publishedDeadlines.note: The FAQ says "The priority application deadline is December 1st." Late applications are considered by each program committee on a space-available basis. Confirm Fall 2027.

timeline.interviews: Interviews are usually held between late January and mid-March.
timeline.decisions: Acceptance notices go out between February and May.

english.note: Applicants whose native language is not English, or whose bachelor's degree is from a non-English institution, must submit official scores from an accepted exam such as TOEFL or IELTS. No minimum scores are given.

applicationFee.note: Applicants request a waiver by sending supporting documents to the Senior Associate Director of Admissions. The page does not limit waivers to US applicants; international applicants should confirm.

documents: Official transcripts from all institutions attended
Course-by-course WES evaluation for degrees from non-US institutions
requirements.note: The FAQ says international students with non-US degrees are particularly encouraged to submit GRE scores.

funding.note: The FAQ says students accepted to a PhD program receive a fellowship covering tuition and fees, with health insurance and a competitive stipend. No stipend amount, year or international coverage is stated.
